name: Molybdenum
description: Molybdenum (CAS 7439-98-7 ), commonly referenced by its symbol Mo, is a refractory transition metal sourced and traded as a primary alloying and catalytic material across industrial supply chains. In metallurgy and chemical processing, it functions as a high-performance strengthener in steel alloys and as a catalytically active component in refining and synthesis operations. In petroleum refining, Mo-based catalysts are used in hydrodesulfurization units to remove sulfur from crude fractions, meeting fuel quality specifications for global distribution. Steel and superalloy manufacturers incorporate molybdenum to improve high-temperature strength and corrosion resistance in structural components, tooling, and aerospace parts for extreme environments. In the chemical industry, molybdenum compounds derived from elemental Mo serve as precursors for oxidation and ammoxidation catalysts used in producing acrylonitrile and formaldehyde. Pigment producers also use molybdenum as a precursor for molybdate-based colorants applied in coatings and plastics, ensuring high durability and color stability in industrial applications. Molybdenum is commercially available as powder, rod, sheet, wire, and sintered parts, with powder being the most common traded form for chemical and metallurgical processing. Standard grades include technical-grade and high-purity specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 99.9% to 99.99% depending on specific end-use requirements.
